ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE SPECIAL ACT ON MANAGEMENT OF HIGH-LEVEL RADIOACTIVE WASTE

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Special Act on Management of High-Level Radioactive Waste and matters necessary for its enforcement.

CHAPTER II HIGH-LEVEL RADIOACTIVE WASTE MANAGEMENT COMMISSION, ETC.

Article 2 (Exclusion, Challenge, and Recusal of Members)
(1) Where a member of the High-Level Radioactive Waste Management Commission (hereinafter referred to as the "Commission") under Article 6 of the Special Act on Management of High-Level Radioactive Waste (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the member shall be excluded from the Commission's deliberation and resolution:
1. Where the member, the member's spouse, or a person who was the member's spouse is a party to the relevant matter, or is a joint holder of rights or joint obligor with a party to that matter;
2. Where the member is or was a relative of a party to the relevant matter;
3. Where the member has provided testimony, statements, advice, research, services, or an appraisal concerning the relevant matter;
4. Where the member or the corporation to which the member belongs is or was an agent of a party to the relevant matter;
5. Where the member is otherwise recognized as having a direct interest in the matter under deliberation.
(2) Where a member has a ground for exclusion specified in any subparagraph of paragraph (1), or there are circumstances that make it difficult to expect fair deliberation and resolution, a party to the matter may challenge the member before the Commission, and the Commission shall decide by resolution whether to accept the challenge. In such cases, the member subject to the challenge shall not participate in that resolution.
(3) Where a member falls under any ground for exclusion specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1), or considers that there are circumstances that make it difficult to expect the member to deliberate fairly, the member shall voluntarily recuse himself or herself from deliberation and resolution on the relevant matter.

Article 3 (Composition and Operation of Sectoral Expert Committees)
(1) Sectoral expert committees under Article 8 (6) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "sectoral expert committees") may be established separately for fields such as sites, storage, and disposal.
(2) Each sectoral expert committee shall consist of not more than 15 members, including one chairperson, with due consideration given to gender.
(3) The members of a sectoral expert committee (hereinafter referred to as "expert members") shall be the following persons, and its chairperson shall be designated by the chairperson of the Commission from among the expert members:
1. Persons with extensive expertise and experience concerning affairs under the jurisdiction of the Commission who are commissioned by the chairperson of the Commission;
2. Employees of relevant institutions designated by the chairperson of the Commission who are nominated by the heads of those institutions.
(4) The chairperson of a sectoral expert committee shall convene and preside over its meetings: Provided, That where the chairperson is unable to perform duties for an unavoidable reason, expert members designated in advance by the chairperson of the sectoral expert committee shall act on the chairperson's behalf in the order of such designation.
(5) Meetings of a sectoral expert committee shall be convened with a majority of its incumbent members present, and resolutions shall be adopted with the affirmative votes of a majority of the members present.
(6) Article 2 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the exclusion, challenge, and recusal of expert members. In such cases, each reference to the "Commission" shall be deemed a reference to a "sectoral expert committee", and each reference to a "member" shall be deemed a reference to an "expert member".

Article 4 (Matters in Meeting Minutes Not Subject to Disclosure)
(1) "Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso to Article 14 (2) of the Act means the following matters:
1. Matters whose disclosure is restricted under other Acts, such as the Official Information Disclosure Act, or matters whose disclosure is recognized as likely to infringe personal privacy;
2. Matters under deliberation concerning matters specified in the subparagraphs of Article 7 (1) of the Act, whose disclosure is recognized as likely to affect fair investigation or deliberation;
3. Other matters whose disclosure is recognized as likely to seriously undermine the fairness of deliberation by the Commission or a sectoral expert committee.
(2) Where the Commission does not disclose all or part of meeting minutes pursuant to the proviso to Article 14 (2) of the Act, it shall post the grounds for nondisclosure and the nondisclosure period on its website, and shall disclose the minutes immediately when the grounds for nondisclosure cease to exist or the nondisclosure period ends.
(3) Matters necessary for disclosure of meeting minutes, other than those provided for in paragraphs (1) and (2), shall be determined by the chairperson of the Commission following a resolution of the Commission.

Article 5 (Detailed Rules for Operation)
Matters necessary for operation of the Commission and sectoral expert committees, other than those provided for in this Decree, shall be determined by the chairperson of the Commission following a resolution of the Commission.

Article 6 (Basic Plan for Management of High-Level Radioactive Waste)
(1) "Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 17 (3) 7 of the Act means the following matters:
1. Matters concerning promotion of public understanding of the management of high-level radioactive waste;
2. Other matters resolved by the Commission for the safe management of high-level radioactive waste.
(2) "Where minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree are changed" in the proviso to Article 17 (5) of the Act means any of the following cases:
1. Where some of the matters under Article 17 (3) 6 and 7 of the Act are changed without changing the purpose and direction of the basic plan for management of high-level radioactive waste under paragraph (2) of that Article (hereinafter referred to as the "basic plan");
2. Where matters that do not affect the purpose and direction of the basic plan are changed and the grounds for the changes are clear;
3. Where simple mistakes, misstatements, omissions, or obvious errors are corrected.

Article 7 (Public Inspection for Formulation of the Basic Plan)
(1) Where the Commission intends to gather public opinions concerning formulation of the basic plan pursuant to the former part of Article 17 (6) of the Act, it shall publicly announce the following matters in the Official Gazette and make the draft basic plan available for public inspection for at least 14 days from the date of the announcement. In such cases, public holidays and Saturdays shall not be counted in the public inspection period:
1. An outline of the draft basic plan;
2. The period and places for public inspection of the draft basic plan (including the Commission's website);
3. The period and methods for submitting opinions on the draft basic plan (including opinions on whether to hold a public hearing under Article 8).
(2) A person having an opinion on the draft basic plan publicly announced and made available for inspection under paragraph (1) may submit the opinion to the Commission during the submission period under subparagraph 3 of that paragraph.
(3) The Commission shall notify each person who submitted an opinion under paragraph (2) of the results of its consideration of that opinion within 30 days from the day following the end of the submission period.

Article 8 (Holding of Public Hearings)
(1) "A request from residents within a scope prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the latter part of Article 17 (6) of the Act means a request by at least 30 residents of a Special Self-Governing City, Special Self-Governing Province (excluding a Special Self-Governing Province having Sis or Guns that are local governments within its jurisdiction), Si, Gun, or autonomous Gu (hereinafter referred to as a "Si/Gun/Gu") in which a high-level radioactive waste management facility (hereinafter referred to as a "management facility") is being constructed or operated, or which has been selected as a site for a management facility.
(2) Where the Commission intends to hold a public hearing pursuant to the latter part of Article 17 (6) of the Act, it shall publicly announce an outline of the draft basic plan, the date, time, and place of the public hearing, etc. at least once each in a daily newspaper (meaning a general daily newspaper registered under Article 9 (1) of the Act on the Promotion of Newspapers, etc. with the entire country as its principal distribution area; hereinafter the same shall apply), in a local newspaper (meaning a general daily newspaper registered under that paragraph with the relevant Si/Gun/Gu as its principal distribution area; hereinafter the same shall apply), and on the Commission's website, no later than 14 days before the hearing date. In such cases, the Commission shall consult in advance concerning the date, time, and place of the public hearing, etc. with the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor (excluding the Governor of a Special Self-Governing Province having Sis or Guns that are local governments within its jurisdiction), Mayor, head of a Gun, or head of a Gu (meaning the head of an autonomous Gu; hereinafter referred to as the "head of a Si/Gun/Gu") having jurisdiction over the relevant Si/Gun/Gu.
(3) Where the grounds under Article 38-2 (2) 2 of the Administrative Procedures Act exist, the Commission may hold an online public hearing.
(4) The Commission shall notify the head of the Si/Gun/Gu for the area subject to the public hearing of the results of the hearing within seven days from the day following the date on which the hearing ends.

Article 9 (Applications for Approval of and Changes to Implementation Plans for Management of High-Level Radioactive Waste)
(1) A high-level radioactive waste management operator under Article 38 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "management operator") shall, pursuant to Article 19 of the Act, formulate an implementation plan for management of high-level radioactive waste (hereinafter referred to as an "implementation plan") containing the following matters and submit it to the Commission for approval:
1. Direction for project implementation;
2. Detailed project plans (including project scale and implementation period);
3. A financing plan.
(2) Where a management operator intends to obtain approval for a change to, or report a change to, matters approved under Article 19 (2) of the Act, it shall submit to the Commission the implementation plan to be changed, accompanied by a document stating the details of and reasons for the change.
(3) "Where minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree are changed" in the proviso to Article 19 (2) of the Act means any of the following cases:
1. Where the project scale specified in the implementation plan is changed within a range of 10 percent;
2. Where the timing of implementation of an individual project is changed within the implementation period specified in the implementation plan;
3. Where matters that do not affect the purpose and direction of the implementation plan are changed and the grounds for the changes are clear;
4. Where simple mistakes, misstatements, omissions, or obvious errors are corrected.

CHAPTER III SITE SUITABILITY SURVEYS AND SELECTION OF SITES FOR MANAGEMENT FACILITIES, ETC.

Article 10 (Methods and Procedures for Applying for Basic Site Suitability Surveys, etc.)
(1) Where the Commission intends to select a site subject to a basic site suitability survey under Article 21 (2) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "site subject to a basic survey"), it shall do so through an open call for applications.
(2) When making an open call for sites subject to basic surveys under paragraph (1), the Commission shall publicly announce the following matters in the Official Gazette and at least two daily newspapers and post them on the Commission's website for at least six months:
1. An outline of the basic site suitability survey (including its purpose, period, and criteria and methods for evaluating its results);
2. Support measures upon selection as a site subject to a basic survey or as a site subject to a detailed survey under Article 21 (1);
3. The period and methods for applying for a basic site suitability survey (including confirmation of local residents' opinions and consent of the local council under the main clause of Article 21 (3) of the Act, and consultation with the heads of Si/Gun/Gu of adjacent local governments under the proviso to that paragraph);
4. Other matters necessary for an open call for selection of sites subject to basic surveys.
(3) Details concerning the open call under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be determined by the chairperson of the Commission following a resolution of the Commission.

Article 11 (Areas Adjacent to Candidate Sites for Basic Surveys)
(1) "Where the requirements prescribed by Presidential Decree are met" in the proviso to Article 21 (3) of the Act means a case where the area within five kilometers of the boundary of a candidate site for which an application for a basic site suitability survey is to be made includes territory under the jurisdiction of a Si/Gun/Gu other than the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over that site.
(2) Where the head of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over a candidate site for a basic survey intends to consult, pursuant to the proviso to Article 21 (3) of the Act, with the head of another adjacent Si/Gun/Gu that meets the requirements under paragraph (1) (hereinafter referred to as an "area adjacent to a basic survey site"), the head may inquire in advance of the Commission whether such an area exists.
(3) The Commission may conduct investigations or surveys to determine whether an area adjacent to a basic survey site under paragraph (2) exists: Provided, That where materials containing the results of investigations or surveys under other statutes or regulations are available, those materials may be used.

Article 12 (Selection of Management Facility Sites)
(1) "Within a scope prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 23 (2) and the former part of Article 23 (3) of the Act means, respectively, within five kilometers of the boundary of the prospective management facility site identified under paragraph (1) of that Article.
(2) Where the Commission selects a management facility site under Article 23 (2) of the Act, it shall notify the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment of that fact and have the management operator apply to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment for designation of the site as a prospective electric power source development project zone under Article 11 of the Electric Power Source Development Promotion Act. <Amended on October 1, 2025>

Article 13 (Scope of Management Facility Host Areas and Surrounding Areas)
"Areas within a scope prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 24 (1) of the Act means the following areas:
1. The territory of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the management facility site (hereinafter referred to as a "management facility host area");
2. The territory of a Si/Gun/Gu other than that specified in subparagraph 1 having jurisdiction over land and island areas situated within five kilometers of the boundary of the management facility site (hereinafter referred to as an "area surrounding a management facility").

Article 14 (Composition of the Support Committee for Management Facility Host Areas)
(1) Not more than six commissioned members of the Support Committee for Management Facility Host Areas under Article 24 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Support Committee") shall be commissioned with consideration given to gender, and three of them shall be persons who reside in or have ties to the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over management facility host areas, etc. under Article 24 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "management facility host areas, etc.").
(2) "Heads of central administrative agencies prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 24 (3) 1 of the Act means the heads designated by the Prime Minister from among the heads of central administrative agencies related to support for the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over management facility host areas, etc., and their number shall not exceed five.

Article 15 (Duties of the Chairperson of the Support Committee)
(1) The chairperson of the Support Committee shall represent the Support Committee and exercise overall control over its affairs.
(2) Where the chairperson of the Support Committee is unable to perform duties for an unavoidable reason, members shall act on the chairperson's behalf in the order designated in advance by the chairperson.

Article 16 (Meetings of the Support Committee)
(1) The chairperson of the Support Committee shall convene and preside over meetings of the Support Committee.
(2) Where the chairperson of the Support Committee intends to convene a meeting, the chairperson shall notify each member of the date, time, place, and agenda no later than seven days before the meeting: Provided, That in urgent circumstances or for another unavoidable reason, such notification may be given no later than the day preceding the meeting.
(3) Meetings of the Support Committee shall be convened with a majority of its incumbent members present, and resolutions shall be adopted with the affirmative votes of a majority of the members present.
(4) Article 2 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the exclusion, challenge, and recusal of Support Committee members. In such cases, each reference to the "Commission" shall be deemed a reference to the "Support Committee", and each reference to a "member" shall be deemed a reference to a "Support Committee member".

Article 17 (Dismissal of Support Committee Members, etc.)
(1) The chairperson of the Support Committee may dismiss a commissioned member under Article 24 (3) of the Act where the member falls under any of the following subparagraphs:
1. Where the member becomes unable to perform duties for an extended period due to physical or mental infirmity, etc.;
2. Where the member has committed misconduct related to duties;
3. Where the member is deemed unsuitable due to neglect of duties, damage to dignity, or other reasons;
4. Where the member fails to recuse despite falling under a ground for exclusion specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2 (1), as applied mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 16 (4), or being deemed to have circumstances that make it difficult to expect impartial deliberation from the member;
5. Where the member expresses an intention to step down because of difficulty in performing duties.
(2) Matters concerning the operation of the Support Committee not provided for in this Decree shall be prescribed by the chairperson of the Support Committee following a resolution of the Support Committee.

Article 18 (Composition of the Working Committee)
(1) The Working Committee under Article 24 (6) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Working Committee") shall consist of not more than 20 members (hereinafter referred to as "Working Committee members"), including one chairperson (hereinafter referred to as the "Working Committee chairperson"), with consideration given to gender.
(2) The chairperson of the Commission shall serve as the Working Committee chairperson, and Working Committee members shall be the following persons:
1. Not more than 10 persons designated, at the request of the Working Committee chairperson, by the heads of the relevant central administrative agencies from among public officials in the Senior Civil Service or equivalent public officials of the central administrative agencies to which members under Article 24 (3) 1 of the Act belong or of central administrative agencies related to agenda items submitted to the Working Committee;
2. One person each designated by the relevant Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayor, or Do Governor (including the governor of a Special Self-Governing Province that contains Sis or Guns constituting local governments within its jurisdiction), from among the deputy mayors or deputy governors of the Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, or Do (including a Special Self-Governing Province that contains Sis or Guns constituting local governments within its jurisdiction) to which the Si/Gun/Gu (excluding Special Self-Governing Cities and Special Self-Governing Provinces) having jurisdiction over management facility host areas, etc. belongs;
3. One person each designated by the relevant head of a Si/Gun/Gu from among the deputy mayor, deputy governor, deputy head of a Gun, or deputy head of a Gu of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over management facility host areas, etc.;
4. One person designated by the management operator from among its officers and employees;
5. Not more than six persons with extensive knowledge and experience concerning nuclear energy or support projects related to nuclear energy, commissioned by the Working Committee chairperson. In such cases, they shall include three persons who reside in or have ties to the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over management facility host areas, etc.
(3) The term of office of Working Committee members under paragraph (2) 5 shall be two years.

Article 19 (Functions of the Working Committee)
The Working Committee shall deliberate on the following matters:
1. Review and coordination of agenda items to be submitted to the Support Committee;
2. Handling of matters delegated by the Support Committee;
3. Other matters that the chairperson of the Support Committee or the Working Committee chairperson deems necessary and submits to a meeting.

Article 20 (Operation of the Working Committee)
(1) The Working Committee shall have one executive secretary to handle its affairs, and the head of the secretariat under Article 15 (1) of the Act shall serve as the executive secretary.
(2) Article 15 and Article 16 (1) through (3) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the operation of the Working Committee. In such cases, each reference to the "chairperson of the Support Committee" shall be deemed a reference to the "Working Committee chairperson", and each reference to the "Support Committee" shall be deemed a reference to the "Working Committee".
(3) Article 2 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the exclusion, challenge, and recusal of Working Committee members. In such cases, each reference to the "Commission" shall be deemed a reference to the "Working Committee", and each reference to a "member" shall be deemed a reference to a "Working Committee member".
(4) The Working Committee chairperson may dismiss a Working Committee member under Article 18 (2) 5 where the member falls under any of the following subparagraphs:
1. Where the member falls under any of the subparagraphs of Article 17 (1), excluding subparagraph 4;
2. Where the member fails to recuse despite falling under a ground for exclusion specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2 (1), as applied mutatis mutandis pursuant to paragraph (3), or being deemed to have circumstances that make it difficult to expect impartial deliberation from the member.

Article 21 (Formulation of Support Plans for Management Facility Host Areas)
(1) When formulating a support plan for management facility host areas under Article 26 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "support plan"), the Commission may request the head of a Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over a site identified under Article 22 (1) of the Act as subject to a detailed site suitability survey (hereinafter referred to as a "site subject to a detailed survey") to submit a request for support.
(2) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu requested to submit a request for support under paragraph (1) shall prepare a request for support for the relevant Si/Gun/Gu and submit it to the Commission within one year from the date the site is confirmed as a site subject to a detailed survey. In such cases, where the jurisdiction of another Si/Gun/Gu lies within five kilometers of the boundary of the site subject to a detailed survey, the head shall consult with the head of that Si/Gun/Gu and jointly prepare and submit a request for support to the Commission.
(3) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu requested to submit a request for support under paragraph (1) may gather residents' opinions by conducting opinion polls, holding public hearings, etc. to prepare the request for support under paragraph (2).
(4) The Commission may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and local governments to submit opinions on the contents of a request for support submitted under paragraph (2). In such cases, the head of an agency requested to submit an opinion shall, unless there are special circumstances, send to the Commission a written opinion on the request for support within six months from the date of receipt of the request for an opinion.
(5) When formulating a support plan, the Commission shall, unless there are special circumstances, reflect the request for support submitted under paragraph (2) and the results of consultation under paragraph (4).
(6) The Commission shall formulate a support plan before the residents' referendum under Article 23 (2) of the Act is held.

Article 22 (Notification of Support Plans)
(1) A support plan finalized under Article 26 (2) of the Act shall take effect from the date on which the site of the management facility is designated and publicly notified as a prospective area for an electric power source development project under Article 11 of the Electric Power Source Development Promotion Act.
(2) The Commission shall notify the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and the heads of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the management facility host area and the area surrounding the management facility of the support plan finalized under Article 26 (2) of the Act within five days from the date the plan takes effect under paragraph (1).

Article 23 (Amendment of Support Plans)
(1) The Commission may amend a support plan upon a request from the heads of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the management facility host area and the area surrounding the management facility, or where the Commission deems amendment unavoidable due to changes in circumstances.
(2) When requesting amendment of a support plan under paragraph (1), the heads of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the management facility host area and the area surrounding the management facility shall submit a request for amendment of support to the Commission: Provided, That where two or more Si/Gun/Gu have jurisdiction over the management facility host area and the area surrounding the management facility, the relevant heads of the Si/Gun/Gu shall consult with one another and jointly submit a request for amendment of support.
(3) Article 21 (4) and (5) shall apply mutatis mutandis to amendments to support plans. In such cases, each reference to a "request for support" shall be deemed a reference to a "request for amendment of support", and "formulating" shall be deemed "amending".
(4) Where the Commission finalizes an amendment to a support plan following deliberation by the Support Committee, it shall notify the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and the heads of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the management facility host area and the area surrounding the management facility of the amended support plan within five days from the date the amendment is finalized.

Article 24 (Formulation of Support Implementation Plans for Management Facility Host Areas)
(1) After being notified of a support plan under Article 22 (2), the heads of relevant central administrative agencies shall formulate annual implementation plans for support for management facility host areas under Article 27 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "support implementation plans") and submit them to the Commission.
(2) Pursuant to Article 27 (2) of the Act, the heads of relevant central administrative agencies shall submit to the Commission the implementation results of the preceding year's support implementation plans and the support implementation plans for the current year by the last day of February each year.
(3) The heads of relevant central administrative agencies shall notify the heads of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the management facility host area and the area surrounding the management facility of the support implementation plans submitted to the Commission under paragraphs (1) and (2).

Article 25 (Contents of Support Implementation Plans)
Support implementation plans shall include the following matters:
1. Names, purposes, and outlines of support projects;
2. Detailed plans for support projects (including matters concerning the scale, contents, implementation period, location, effects, etc. of the projects);
3. Annual or quarterly funding support plans;
4. Other matters deemed necessary by the heads of relevant central administrative agencies concerning support projects.

Article 26 (Amendment of Support Implementation Plans)
(1) Where deemed unavoidable due to an amendment to a support plan, changes in circumstances, etc., the head of a relevant central administrative agency may amend a support implementation plan. In such cases, the head of the relevant central administrative agency shall, without delay, submit to the Commission the support implementation plan proposed to be amended, attaching a document stating the contents of and reasons for the amendment.
(2) The head of the relevant central administrative agency shall notify the heads of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the management facility host area and the area surrounding the management facility of the amended support implementation plan submitted to the Commission under paragraph (1).

Article 27 (Amount of Special Support Grants for Management Facility Host Areas, etc.)
(1) The amount of special support grants for management facility host areas, etc. under Article 28 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "special support grants") to be provided to the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the management facility host area and the area surrounding the management facility shall be no less than the amount under Article 21 of the Enforcement Decree of the Special Act on Support for Areas Hosting Intermediate- and Low-Level Radioactive Waste Disposal Facilities, and shall be determined by the Commission following deliberation by the Support Committee, taking into consideration the scale of the management facility, construction costs, etc.
(2) Where the Commission determines the amount of special support grants under paragraph (1), it shall notify the management operator of the determination and have the management operator provide those special support grants to the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the management facility host area and the area surrounding the management facility pursuant to Article 28 (1) of the Act.

Article 28 (Methods of Allocating Special Support Grants)
Where two or more Si/Gun/Gu have jurisdiction over the management facility host area and the area surrounding the management facility, special support grants under Article 27 (1) shall be allocated as follows:
1. An amount equivalent to 40 percent of the special support grants shall be allocated in proportion to each Si/Gun/Gu's share of the area of land and islands within five kilometers of the boundary of the management facility site;
2. An amount equivalent to 30 percent of the special support grants shall be allocated in proportion to each Si/Gun/Gu's share of the population of the land and island areas within five kilometers of the boundary of the management facility site;
3. An amount equivalent to 20 percent of the special support grants shall be allocated to the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the management facility host area;
4. An amount equivalent to 10 percent of the special support grants shall be allocated according to criteria determined by the Commission, taking into consideration local conditions, including the level of regional development and equity in the allocation of support grants among regions.

Article 29 (Timing of Provision of Special Support Grants)
(1) A management operator notified under Article 27 (2) shall provide special support grants to the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the management facility host area and the area surrounding the management facility within 30 days from the date of notification: Provided, That where the Commission decides that the grants are to be provided in installments, each installment shall be provided within 30 days from the date of notification to provide that installment of the special support grants.
(2) Provision of special support grants under Article 27 (1) shall be completed by the day preceding the date on which operation of the high-level radioactive waste disposal facility under Article 17 (1) of the Act commences.

Article 30 (Suspension of Support for Host Areas)
(1) Where support has been provided under Articles 26 through 28 of the Act and the construction or operation of a management facility has been suspended for an aggregate of at least 6 months within a 12-month period due to circumstances for which the State or the management operator cannot be held responsible, the Commission may require the management operator and the heads of relevant central administrative agencies to suspend support for the relevant management facility host area and area surrounding a management facility.
(2) Where support is suspended under paragraph (1), the head of a Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the management facility host area and area surrounding a management facility shall, if any amount received as support, including special support grants under Article 27 (1), remains unspent, suspend the relevant project and refrain from using that amount. Provided, That, where necessary to minimize losses or costs resulting from suspension of the project, the head may implement necessary projects with the Commission's approval.
(3) Where the grounds for suspension of support under paragraph (1) have been resolved, the Commission shall require the management operator and the heads of relevant central administrative agencies to resume support for the management facility host area and area surrounding a management facility.

Article 31 (Special Account for Host Area Support Projects) The term "projects prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 29 (4) 5 of the Act means the following projects:
1. Surveys and research related to support projects for management facility host areas, etc.;
2. Expansion and management of facilities and equipment for radiological disaster prevention;
3. Support for the establishment and operation of civilian environmental monitoring bodies concerning radiation safety.

Article 32 (Operation of Underground Research Facilities, etc.)
(1) To efficiently operate the underground research facilities under Article 30 (1) and (2) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "underground research facilities"), the Commission shall formulate an operation plan for underground research facilities every 5 years, with a planning period of at least 10 years.
(2) The operation plan for underground research facilities under paragraph (1) shall include the following matters:
1. Goals for the operation of underground research facilities and directions for priority technology development;
2. Analysis of technology gaps with advanced countries and strategies to address them;
3. Timeframes for the realization of key technologies;
4. Joint research with domestic and foreign research institutions, organizations, etc. related to disposal technologies concerning underground research facilities;
5. Plans for the utilization of technology development outcomes;
6. Measures for publicity concerning underground research facilities and regional cooperation;
7. Other matters deemed necessary by the Commission.

Article 33 (Revocation of Selection of a Management Facility Site) The phrase "within the scope prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 31 (4) of the Act means within 5 kilometers of the boundary of the management facility site.

CHAPTER IV MANAGEMENT OF HIGH-LEVEL RADIOACTIVE WASTE, ETC.

Article 34 (Development of Infrastructure for Management of High-Level Radioactive Waste)
(1) The infrastructure development plan for management of high-level radioactive waste under Article 33 (2) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "infrastructure development plan") shall be consistent with the basic plan and shall include the following matters:
1. Basic goals and directions for technology development;
2. Matters concerning the training of specialized personnel (including medium- and long-term supply and demand forecasts);
3. Matters concerning the development of and support for related industries;
4. Investment amounts and financing plans;
5. Other matters necessary for the development of infrastructure for management of high-level radioactive waste.
(2) Where a management operator seeks approval for an amendment to an infrastructure development plan pursuant to the main clause of Article 33 (3) of the Act, it shall submit to the Commission the infrastructure development plan to be amended, accompanied by documents stating the details of and grounds for the amendment.
(3) Upon receiving a request for approval or approval of an amendment under the main clause of Article 33 (3) of the Act, the Commission shall notify the management operator of whether approval is granted within 60 days from the date of receipt of the request. Provided, That, where the Commission requires supplementary data or there are other special circumstances, it may extend that period only once by up to 60 days.
(4) The phrase "when amending minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso to Article 33 (3) of the Act means any of the following cases:
1. Where the investment amount under paragraph (1) 4 is changed within a range of 10/100;
2. Where a matter that does not affect the purposes or directions of the infrastructure development plan and for which the grounds for amendment are clear is amended;
3. Where a simple mistake, clerical error, omission, or manifest error is corrected.

Article 35 (Technology Development Projects for Safe Management of High-Level Radioactive Waste)
(1) The Commission may implement the following technology development projects pursuant to Article 34 (1) of the Act:
1. Assessment of trends and surveys of demand for technologies for management of high-level radioactive waste (hereinafter referred to as "management technology");
2. Research and development, evaluation, and utilization of management technology;
3. Transfer of management technology and exchange of information;
4. Other projects necessary for the development of management technology.
(2) When incorporating the outcomes of technology development into the basic plan pursuant to Article 34 (2) of the Act, the Commission shall take the following matters into account:
1. The content and long-term effects of the relevant management technology;
2. The economic feasibility and applicability in the field of the relevant management technology;
3. The effects of the relevant management technology on the economy, society, and the environment;
4. International trends and stakeholder opinions.
(3) The term "institutions or organizations prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 34 (3) of the Act means the following institutions or organizations:
1. National and public research institutions;
2. Specific research institutions under Article 2 of the Specific Research Institutions Support Act;
3. Government-funded science and technology research institutions under Article 2 of the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Science and Technology Research Institutions, etc.;
4. The Korea Institute of Energy Technology Evaluation and Planning under Article 13 of the Energy Act;
5. The National Research Foundation of Korea under the National Research Foundation of Korea Act;
6. Corporations established under special Acts;
7. Institutions established as nonprofit corporations under Article 32 of the Civil Act that possess dedicated personnel and expertise related to management technology.

Article 36 (Projects for Training Specialized Personnel)
(1) The scope of projects for training personnel specialized in management technology pursuant to Article 35 (1) of the Act shall be as follows:
1. Education and training to develop specialized personnel and improve skills in each specific field of high-level radioactive waste management;
2. Development and dissemination of education and training programs for specialized personnel;
3. Projects for analysis of the supply and demand of specialized personnel and establishment of databases;
4. Strengthening cooperation with academia, industry, and public institutions for training specialized personnel;
5. Projects for promoting domestic and international exchanges of specialized personnel.
(2) The term "institution prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 35 (2) 4 of the Act means the Korea Radioactive Waste Agency under Article 18 (1) of the Radioactive Waste Management Act.
(3) A person seeking designation as an institution for training specialized personnel under Article 35 (2) of the Act shall meet the following requirements:
1. Have a business plan, evaluation plan, and operating regulations necessary to perform duties as an institution for training specialized personnel;
2. Have educational facilities necessary to perform duties as an institution for training specialized personnel;
3. Have specialized instructors necessary to perform duties as an institution for training specialized personnel.
(4) The Commission shall determine and publicly notify the details of the designation requirements under paragraph (3).
(5) A person seeking designation as an institution for training specialized personnel under Article 35 (2) of the Act shall submit to the Commission an application for designation as an institution for training specialized personnel in the Attached Form, accompanied by the following documents:
1. An education and training project plan and an evaluation plan;
2. A statement of the educational facilities and specialized instructors secured;
3. A plan for financing the operating expenses of education and training;
4. Operating regulations concerning education, training, etc.
(6) Upon receiving an application for designation under paragraph (5), the Commission shall verify the certificate of registered corporate matters (applicable only to corporations) through the joint use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act.
(7) Where the Commission designates an institution for training specialized personnel pursuant to Article 35 (2) of the Act, it shall post that fact on its website without delay. The same shall apply where it revokes a designation pursuant to Article 35 (3) of the Act.

Article 37 (Formulation and Amendment of Facility Plans for On-Site Storage Facilities)
(1) A plan (hereinafter referred to as a "facility plan") for spent nuclear fuel storage facilities within nuclear power plant sites under Article 36 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "on-site storage facilities") shall include the following matters:
1. The purposes of installation and uses of on-site storage facilities;
2. An overview of on-site storage facilities that includes the following matters:
(a) The storage capacity of the on-site storage facilities;
(b) The location and area of the on-site storage facilities;
(c) The storage method and construction period of the on-site storage facilities;
(d) Plans for compliance of the on-site storage facilities with the Nuclear Safety Act;
(e) The operating period of the on-site storage facilities and plans for removal of spent nuclear fuel;
3. Investment amounts and financing plans;
4. The results of collecting opinions under Article 36 (4) of the Act.
(2) Where a power reactor operator under Article 22 (1) of the Nuclear Safety Act (hereinafter referred to as a "power reactor operator") seeks approval for an amendment to a facility plan pursuant to the main clause of Article 36 (2) of the Act, it shall submit the facility plan to be amended, accompanied by documents stating the details of and grounds for the amendment (including documents explaining the necessity of the amendment).
(3) Upon receiving a request for approval or approval of an amendment to a facility plan under the main clause of Article 36 (2) of the Act, the Commission shall notify the power reactor operator of whether approval is granted within 90 days from the date of receipt of the request. Provided, That, where the Commission requires supplementary data or there are other special circumstances, it may extend that period only once by up to 60 days.
(4) The phrase "when amending minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso to Article 36 (2) of the Act means any of the following cases:
1. Where the construction period under paragraph (1) 2 (c) is shortened or extended by up to 1 year. In such cases, an extension shall be limited to 1 occasion;
2. Where the investment amount under paragraph (1) 3 is changed within a range of 10/100;
3. Where a matter that does not affect the purposes or directions of the facility plan and for which the grounds for amendment are clear is amended;
4. Where a simple mistake, clerical error, omission, or manifest error is corrected.

Article 38 (Scope of Areas Surrounding On-Site Storage Facilities, Public Notice and Inspection, etc.)
(1) The term "areas within the scope prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the former part of the portion of Article 36 (4) of the Act other than its subparagraphs means the areas of Sis/Guns/Gus having jurisdiction over land and island areas within a radius of 5 kilometers from the point where an on-site storage facility is to be installed (hereinafter referred to as the "storage facility installation point"), such Si/Gun/Gu areas being hereinafter referred to as "areas surrounding on-site storage facilities".
(2) To collect opinions on a facility plan from residents of areas surrounding on-site storage facilities (hereinafter referred to as "residents of surrounding areas" in this Chapter) pursuant to Article 36 (4) of the Act, a power reactor operator shall prepare in advance a draft facility plan (excluding the matters under Article 37 (1) 4; hereinafter the same shall apply) and forward it to the following persons:
1. The Commission;
2. The head of a Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over areas surrounding on-site storage facilities (hereinafter referred to as the "head of a Si/Gun/Gu governing surrounding areas" in this Chapter);
3. The heads of other central administrative agencies related to the installation of on-site storage facilities.
(3) Where a power reactor operator intends to collect opinions from residents of surrounding areas pursuant to Article 36 (4) 1 of the Act, it shall publicly announce the following matters at least once each in a daily newspaper and a local newspaper and make the draft facility plan available for public inspection by residents of surrounding areas for a period of at least 20 days but not more than 40 days. In such cases, public holidays and Saturdays shall not be counted toward the public inspection period:
1. An overview of the draft facility plan;
2. The period and locations for public inspection of the draft facility plan [including the websites of the Sis/Guns/Gus having jurisdiction over areas surrounding on-site storage facilities (hereinafter referred to as "Sis/Guns/Gus governing surrounding areas" in this Chapter) and of the power reactor operator];
3. The period and methods for submitting opinions on the draft facility plan (including opinions on whether to hold a public hearing under Article 40).
(4) Residents of surrounding areas who have opinions on the draft facility plan made available for public inspection under paragraph (3) may submit their opinions to the power reactor operator during the submission period under subparagraph 3 of that paragraph.
(5) Before making a public announcement under paragraph (3), a power reactor operator shall hear the opinions of the head of a Si/Gun/Gu governing surrounding areas on the public inspection period and locations, etc. and determine those matters accordingly, and shall establish at least 1 public inspection location in each Si/Gun/Gu governing surrounding areas.

Article 39 (Briefings and Discussion Meetings)
(1) A power reactor operator shall hold briefings and discussion meetings (hereinafter referred to as "briefings, etc.") for residents of surrounding areas under Article 36 (4) 2 of the Act within 90 days from the date on which the draft facility plan is transmitted pursuant to Article 38 (2). In such cases, details such as the number, dates, times, and venues of the briefings, etc. shall be determined through consultation between the power reactor operator and the head of a Si/Gun/Gu governing surrounding areas.
(2) Where a power reactor operator intends to hold briefings, etc. under paragraph (1), the operator shall publish an outline of the facility plan for the on-site storage facility, the dates, times, and venues of the briefings, etc., and other relevant matters at least once each in a daily newspaper and a local newspaper and on the power reactor operator's website no later than 14 days before the date of the briefings, etc.
(3) Where briefings, etc. publicly announced under paragraph (2) could not be held, or were held but could not proceed normally, for reasons for which the power reactor operator cannot be held responsible, the operator may, in consultation with the head of a Si/Gun/Gu governing surrounding areas, hold briefings, etc. using an information and communications network (hereinafter referred to as "online briefings, etc.").
(4) Where a power reactor operator intends to hold online briefings, etc. under paragraph (3), the operator shall publicly announce the reasons for holding online briefings, etc., the period and methods for submission of opinions by persons wishing to submit opinions at the online briefings, etc., and other relevant matters. In such cases, paragraph (2) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the methods of public announcement.

Article 40 (Holding of Public Hearings)
(1) In any of the following cases, a power reactor operator shall hold a public hearing for residents of surrounding areas before the expiry of six months from the date on which the draft facility plan is transmitted pursuant to Article 38 (2). In such cases, the public hearing shall be held after the briefings, etc. under Article 39 (1) have concluded:
1. Where at least 30 residents of surrounding areas have submitted opinions that a public hearing is necessary after the public inspection under Article 38 (3);
2. Where at least five but fewer than 30 residents of surrounding areas have submitted opinions that a public hearing is necessary after the public inspection under Article 38 (3), and those residents constitute at least 50 percent of the total number of residents of surrounding areas who have submitted opinions on the draft facility plan.
(2) Where a power reactor operator intends to hold a public hearing under paragraph (1), the operator shall publish an outline of the project, the date, time, and venue of the public hearing, and other relevant matters at least once each in a daily newspaper and a local newspaper and on the power reactor operator's website no later than 14 days before the date of the public hearing. In such cases, the operator shall consult in advance with the head of a Si/Gun/Gu governing surrounding areas concerning the date, time, venue, etc. of the public hearing.
(3) Where a public hearing publicly announced under paragraph (2) has, on at least three occasions, either been unable to be held or been held but broken up without proceeding normally, for reasons for which the power reactor operator cannot be held responsible, the operator may hold an online public hearing using an information and communications network.
(4) Where a power reactor operator intends to hold an online public hearing under paragraph (3), the operator shall publicly announce the reasons for holding the online public hearing, the period and methods for submission of opinions by persons wishing to submit opinions at the online public hearing, and other relevant matters. In such cases, paragraph (2) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the methods of public announcement.

Article 41 (Criteria for Approval of Facility Plans)
Upon receiving a request for approval of a facility plan or for approval of an amendment thereto under the main clause of Article 36 (2) of the Act, the Commission shall determine whether to grant approval by comprehensively considering the following matters:
1. The necessity of installing the on-site storage facility;
2. Consistency with the basic plan;
3. The appropriateness of the calculation of storage capacity under Article 37 (1) 2 (a);
4. The thoroughness of the process of gathering opinions from residents of surrounding areas under Articles 38 through 40.

Article 42 (Support for Areas Surrounding On-Site Storage Facilities)
(1) The term "territorial units prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 37 (2) 2 of the Act means Eup/Myeon/Dong.
(2) The term "other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as the scale of financial resources for each year" in Article 37 (2) 3 of the Act means the following matters:
1. Principles and basic directions for support for areas surrounding on-site storage facilities;
2. The annual scale of support grants under Article 37 (2) 1 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "support grants" in this Chapter) and plans for securing them;
3. Other matters the Commission deems important concerning support for areas surrounding on-site storage facilities.

Article 43 (Formulation of Support Project Plans for Areas Surrounding On-Site Storage Facilities)
(1) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu governing surrounding areas shall formulate and implement each year a support project plan for areas surrounding on-site storage facilities (hereinafter referred to as a "surrounding area support project plan" in this Chapter) that includes the following matters, pursuant to Article 37 (4) of the Act:
1. The purposes and details of support projects for areas surrounding on-site storage facilities (hereinafter referred to as "surrounding area support projects" in this Chapter);
2. The implementation periods and expected effects of surrounding area support projects;
3. Annual investment plans for surrounding area support projects;
4. The implementation results of surrounding area support projects for the preceding year.
(2) Details for each type of surrounding area support project under Article 37 (5) of the Act shall be as specified in attached Table 1.
(3) When formulating a surrounding area support project plan under paragraph (1), the head of a Si/Gun/Gu governing surrounding areas shall have it deliberated upon by the Resident Support Project Deliberation Committee under Article 45.
(4) Before formulating a surrounding area support project plan, the head of a Si/Gun/Gu governing surrounding areas shall hold briefings, etc. for residents of surrounding areas at least once.
(5) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu governing surrounding areas shall submit the results of surrounding area support projects to the Commission within 20 days after the end of each quarter.

Article 44 (Methods of Distributing Support Grants to Si/Gun/Gu Governing Surrounding Areas)
(1) Support grants shall be distributed to Si/Gun/Gu governing surrounding areas by the following methods:
1. An amount equivalent to 40 percent of the support grants shall be distributed in proportion to the respective shares of the Si/Gun/Gu governing surrounding areas in the total area of mainland and islands within a radius of five kilometers from the storage facility installation point;
2. An amount equivalent to 30 percent of the support grants shall be distributed in proportion to the respective shares of the Si/Gun/Gu governing surrounding areas in the population of the mainland and island areas within a radius of five kilometers from the storage facility installation point;
3. An amount equivalent to 20 percent of the support grants shall be distributed to the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the storage facility installation point;
4. An amount equivalent to 10 percent of the support grants shall be distributed in accordance with criteria determined by the Commission in consideration of local conditions, such as the level of local development and equity in the distribution of support grants among areas.
(2) Support grants distributed to Si/Gun/Gu governing surrounding areas under paragraph (1) shall be distributed as support grants for each territorial unit under Article 37 (2) 2 of the Act by the following methods:
1. An amount equivalent to 70 percent of the support grants distributed to a Si/Gun/Gu governing surrounding areas shall be distributed to Eup/Myeon/Dong areas encompassing mainland and island areas within a radius of five kilometers from the storage facility installation point;
2. An amount equivalent to 30 percent of the support grants distributed to a Si/Gun/Gu governing surrounding areas shall be distributed to Eup/Myeon/Dong areas encompassing mainland and island areas outside a radius of five kilometers from the storage facility installation point.

Article 45 (Establishment of Resident Support Project Deliberation Committees)
(1) A Resident Support Project Deliberation Committee shall be established in each Si/Gun/Gu governing surrounding areas to deliberate on surrounding area support project plans. In such cases, matters concerning the composition and operation of the Resident Support Project Deliberation Committee shall be prescribed by ordinance of the relevant Si/Gun/Gu.
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), where a Regional Committee for Deliberation on Surrounding Area Support Projects has been established under Article 3 (2) of the Act on Support for Areas Surrounding Power Plants, that Regional Committee may take the place of the Resident Support Project Deliberation Committee required to be established under paragraph (1).

Article 46 (Suspension of Surrounding Area Support Projects)
Article 30 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the suspension of surrounding area support projects. In such cases, each reference to "management operator" shall be construed as "power reactor operator", and each reference to "management facility host area and area surrounding a management facility" shall be construed as "areas surrounding on-site storage facilities".

Article 47 (Use of Funds)
(1) The term "projects prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 39 (1) of the Act means the following projects:
1. Projects for the management of high-level radioactive waste (hereinafter referred to as "high-level radioactive waste management projects");
2. Preparation for permits, authorizations, etc. relating to the construction and operation of management facilities;
3. Construction and operation of underground research facilities;
4. Management technology development projects;
5. Projects for training specialized personnel under Article 35 of the Act;
6. Planning, evaluation, and management projects to implement high-level radioactive waste management projects efficiently.
(2) The term "projects prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 39 (2) of the Act means technology development projects under Article 34 (2) of the Act.

CHAPTER V SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 48 (Collection and Distribution of Fees)
(1) The fees under Article 40 (1) of the Act shall be the amounts publicly notified by the Commission following deliberation by the Support Committee.
(2) Where a management operator brings high-level radioactive waste into a management facility under Article 40 (1) of the Act, the management operator shall also pay the fees under paragraph (1).
(3) The term "ratio prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 40 (2) of the Act means 75 percent.
(4) Where two or more Si/Gun/Gu have jurisdiction over a management facility host area and an area surrounding a management facility, the fees accruing to the competent local governments under Article 40 (2) of the Act shall be distributed by the methods specified in the subparagraphs of Article 28. In such cases, each reference to "special support grants" shall be construed as "fees".
(5) A management operator shall, by November 30 each year, investigate the expected quantities of high-level radioactive waste to be brought in during each quarter of the following three years and notify the heads of Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the management facility host area and the area surrounding the management facility.

Article 49 (Procedures for Allocation of Fees)
(1) A management operator shall separately establish and operate an account for collecting fees under Article 40 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "collection account") and an account for managing fees accruing to the management operator under paragraph (2) of that Article (hereinafter referred to as the "management account").
(2) Of the amounts deposited in the collection account (including interest income), the management operator shall remit an amount (including interest income) corresponding to the ratio under Article 48 (3) to the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the management facility host area and the area surrounding the management facility, and transfer and allocate the remainder to the management account. In such cases, the amounts to be remitted and allocated shall be determined on the basis of high-level radioactive waste for which delivery to the management facility and collection of fees have been completed by the last day of each quarter.
(3) A management operator shall make the remittances and allocations under paragraph (2) on a quarterly basis within five days from the first day of the following quarter: Provided, That, where necessary, remittances and allocations may also be made during the relevant quarter.
(4) Where a management operator has remitted funds to Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the management facility host area and the area surrounding the management facility under paragraph (2), the operator shall notify the heads of those Si/Gun/Gu of the details within five days from the date of remittance.

Article 50 (Support Projects by Management Operators)
(1) A management operator may implement support projects under attached Table 2 for the management facility host area and the area surrounding the management facility, using a portion of the fees allocated under Article 49 (2) (including income from their management) as financial resources. In such cases, where two or more Si/Gun/Gu have jurisdiction over the management facility host area and the area surrounding the management facility, the management operator shall distribute the financial resources by the methods specified in the subparagraphs of Article 28 and implement the support projects.
(2) The implementation period for support projects under paragraph (1) shall be the period of operation of the management facility.

Article 51 (Orders to Take Measures Issued to Generators of High-Level Radioactive Waste, etc.)
(1) When issuing an order under Article 42 (1) of the Act to a generator of high-level radioactive waste or a management operator, the Commission shall do so in writing specifying the following matters:
1. Details of the failure to fulfill an obligation;
2. The content of the order;
3. The period for compliance with the order.
(2) Where the Commission finds that compliance with an order under paragraph (1) cannot be completed within the compliance period under paragraph (1) 3 due to a natural disaster or other unavoidable circumstances, it may, upon application by the recipient of the order, extend the compliance period only once for a period not exceeding the original compliance period.
(3) A person who has received an order under paragraph (1) shall, upon complying with the order, notify the Commission of the results of compliance without delay.

Article 52 (Entrustment of Duties)
(1) The term "duties prescribed by Presidential Decree" in subparagraph 3 of Article 44 of the Act means the following duties:
1. Construction and operation of underground research facilities under Article 30 (1) and (2) of the Act;
2. Development of technologies for the safe management of high-level radioactive waste under Article 34 (1) of the Act.
(2) The Commission shall entrust the duties under subparagraphs 1 through 3 of Article 44 of the Act to a management operator pursuant to that Article.

Article 53 (Administrative Fines)
The criteria for imposing administrative fines under Article 50 of the Act shall be as specified in attached Table 3.

Articles 2 through 5: Omitted.

(1) through (4): Omitted.

In Article 12 (2), each occurrence of "Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy" shall be replaced by "Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment".
